close_reason: Both children PKIX-fmtv.12.1 and PKIX-fmtv.12.2 closed. Mailbox binding shipped in pkix-identity (.12.1, 2026-05-12) and verify_smime_signer/verify_smime_recipient wrappers shipped in pkix-chain (.12.2, 2026-05-13). epic_closeable=true confirmed.
description:
**Retargeted 2026-05-11 per `.3` decision (option B):** binding code lives in new `pkix-identity` crate; pkix-chain ships the thin wrappers.

## In `pkix-identity` (fills scaffold stub)

Implement `verify_mailbox(cert: &Certificate, mailbox: &MailboxName) -> Result<(), IdentityError>`:

- Parse leaf's SubjectAlternativeName extension; iterate `GeneralName` entries.
- For each `GeneralName::Rfc822Name(addr)`: apply RFC 5280 §4.2.1.6 + RFC 822 matching against `mailbox`:
  - **Local-part** is case-sensitive by default (per RFC 5321 §2.4 — local-part case-sensitivity is left to the receiving domain; we choose case-sensitive for safety).
  - **Domain part** case-insensitive (per RFC 1035 / RFC 5321).
- For each `GeneralName::OtherName { type_id: id-on-SmtpUTF8Mailbox, value }`: per RFC 8398 §3:
  - Decode `value` as UTF-8 mailbox.
  - Same local-part / domain handling but on UTF-8 (not ASCII).
  - U-label/A-label domain normalization via `idna`.
- If any matches: `Ok(())`. If no SAN entries match (or SAN missing): `Err(IdentityError::NoMatchingMailbox)` or `MissingSan`.

Also implement `MailboxName::parse` constructor with input validation (RFC 5322 syntax, optional internationalized-mailbox handling).

## In `pkix-chain`

Ship two new public functions:

```rust
pub fn verify_smime_signer(
    chain:      &[Certificate],
    anchors:    &[TrustAnchor],
    mailbox:    &MailboxName<'_>,    // from pkix-identity
    policy:     &ValidationPolicy,   // typically BasicSmimeProfile.policy(now)
    verifier:   &impl SignatureVerifier,
    revocation: &impl RevocationChecker,
) -> Result<ValidatedPath, VerifyError>;

pub fn verify_smime_recipient(
    chain:      &[Certificate],
    anchors:    &[TrustAnchor],
    mailbox:    &MailboxName<'_>,
    policy:     &ValidationPolicy,
    verifier:   &impl SignatureVerifier,
    revocation: &impl RevocationChecker,
) -> Result<ValidatedPath, VerifyError>;
```

Bodies:
1. `verify_chain(...)?` (existing).
2. `pkix_identity::verify_mailbox(&chain[0], mailbox)?` (new).
3. `Ok(ValidatedPath)`.

The signer/recipient distinction lives in the `ValidationPolicy` (keyUsage: digitalSignature for signer vs keyEncipherment for recipient — set by the caller via `BasicSmimeProfile` or downstream `SmimeProfile`s in `pkix-profiles-cabf`).

`VerifyError` gets new variants for `MailboxMismatch`, `MalformedMailbox`.

Whether both signer and recipient wrappers ship in v0.x is per `.7` decision.

## Tests

- Plain ASCII mailbox: `alice@example.com` matches SAN `rfc822Name=alice@example.com`.
- Case sensitivity: `Alice@example.com` does NOT match SAN `alice@example.com` (local-part). `alice@Example.com` DOES match SAN `alice@example.com` (domain).
- Internationalized: SAN otherName SmtpUTF8Mailbox `用户@example.com` matches input `用户@example.com`.
- Mixed: SAN with both rfc822Name (ASCII) and otherName (UTF-8) variants; verify both code paths.
- SAN missing → error.

## Blocks on

- New scaffold child (creates pkix-identity with API stubs).
- `.7` (decides whether both signer and recipient wrappers ship).
title: Implement RFC 5280/8398 mailbox binding in pkix-identity + verify_smime_signer/recipient wrappers in pkix-chain
